new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check:, PDF page 20 = Oceania 19(2) p. 110 (running head 'DISTRIBUTION OF LANGUAGES', last paragraph before 'PART II. GRAMMAR'). extracted text gives exactly: 'Accent is rather variable; where it does not fall on the antepenultimate, it is marked in the vocabularies and sentences. Some of the languages have a musical intonation; none, however, employs tone with a semantic significance. The above outline of the phonetic system of the Central Highlands languages will serve the purposes of the present paper.' Also at line 1512 of. Verbatim, including the spaced semicolons. Context read: Part I (pp. 104-110) is Capell's own field phonetics from a 1947 survey; p. 107 states 'Part I rests e…
new_statements.rule_in_words: For the Central Highlands languages as a group (Gende included), accent falls by default on the antepenultimate syllable; it is 'rather variable', and words whose accent is elsewhere are individually marked; no lexical tone.
new_statements.exceptions: 'Accent is rather variable'; wherever it is not antepenultimate Capell marks it in the word lists (no rule given for the deviations). No language of the survey uses tone semantically.
new_statements.domain_note: Blanket characterisation of the phonetic system of ALL Central Highlands languages in Capell's survey (Gende is listed in his Chimbu Group, p. 106, and he states that vocabularies were worked out only for Kuman and Gende), not a Gende-specific statement; word level (vocabulary citation forms and sentences). Burgmann 1953: 264, relaying Aufenanger, says Capell's Gende material needs checking and lists several errors in his Gende forms.
new_statements.identity_note: Capell's 'Gende' (Chimbu Group, Bundi area, Oceania 1948-49) and Aufenanger's Gende (Bundi-Nombri dialect spoken at the Bundi mission station) are the same language as gend1249; no separate dialect glottocode exists. The quoted accent statement is a group-level generalisation over all Central Highlands languages in Capell's survey, not a description of Gende alone.
